I5.quote: Metal organic frameworks (MOFs) are a class of porous organic-inorganic crystalline materials that have attracted much attention as H2 storage devices and catalytic supports.

notes: Catalysis paper: Ni nanoparticles from pyrolysed Ni-MOF-74, tested in thermal hydrogenation of olefins in EtOH at 30 C. No H2 uptake value anywhere, so coded no_conditions_stated per the I1 rule. Not theoretical_only (experimental work). Not electrochemical: the 'Electrocatalysts' banner on page 1 is a journal section label, and the paper has no electrolyte, electrode or electrochemical measurement. TPD-MS (Figure S2, m/z 2 and 16) records gases evolved during MOF decomposition, not uptake. Not a review or patent; record.json is_retracted is false and no retraction notice in the PDF; the paper makes no statement that its data were published before.
